metadata.title: Transforming Data Annotation with AI Agents: A Review of Architectures, Reasoning, Applications, and Impact
metadata.abstract_summary: Surveys the architectures, reasoning patterns, evaluation metrics and deployment trade-offs (cascade routing, drift monitoring) of AI agents used for data annotation.

sections.heading: Claims
sections.text:
What the paper proposes or defines, as extracted (section, page):
- **Agent-type task taxonomy** (category B) - Classifies annotation agents into rule-based, model-based reflex, goal-based, utility-based, and learning types, each matched to task characteristics. (section 4.2. Classification of AI Agents, p. 11)
  > Rule-Based Agents: Operate on predefined conditional logic and excel at structured annotation tasks with clear decision boundaries.
- **Planner-annotator-checker workflow** (category B) - Proposes an agent-centric workflow model with planner, annotator, and quality checker roles, validated against Self-Refine and ActiveLLM. (section 2.3. Limitations of the Existing Surveys, p. 6)
  > it proposes an agent-centric workflow model with planner, annotator and quality checker roles, and validates the model with concrete systems such as Self-Refine and ActiveLLM.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text:
- **Agent-type task taxonomy**: Rule-based agents handle structured validation; model-based reflex agents handle sequential context; goal-based agents decompose projects and orchestrate active learning; utility-based agents balance confidence, cost, expected gains; learning agents adapt from feedback.
- **Planner-annotator-checker workflow**: Planner decomposes annotation tasks; annotator generates labels; quality checker audits outputs; roles run as a closed loop that plans, labels, and self-audits continuously, escalating failures for re-annotation.
- **Role-based ensemble orchestrator**: Orchestrator performs normalization, intent detection, task planning, queuing; parameter extractor and API mapper route tasks to ingest, labeling, consensus agents; annotation services API handles labeling, review, messaging, metrics; tool calls support external interactions.
- **Cascade model routing**: Front-line cheap models or heuristics accept easy items; hard items escalate to frontier LLMs. Related hybrid offloading runs lightweight models on-device and offloads complex tasks to cloud.
- **Agent performance metric suite**: Throughput measured against human benchmarks; quality via gold-standard comparison and consistency; agreement via precision and Cohen's kappa; cost per call and completion time; trust via user override patterns.
- **Drift monitoring with HITL**: Dashboards track human override frequency and error pattern trends; adaptive monitoring detects subtle degradation; continuous learning systems with HITL oversight prevent compounding model errors in dynamic environments.

sections.heading: Evidence & Limits
sections.text:
- Evidence the authors report:
  - Agent-type task taxonomy: Taxonomy applied to annotation task examples in Section 4.2; no new experiment.
  - Planner-annotator-checker workflow: Model validated against concrete systems Self-Refine and ActiveLLM.
  - Role-based ensemble orchestrator: Described as an end-to-end role-based ensemble workflow in Figure 5; no quantitative experiment.
  - Cascade model routing: Section 10.6 reports hybrid local-cloud offloading achieving 50-80% latency reductions and up to 89% cost savings.
  - Agent performance metric suite: Table 6 compiles metrics across studies: Success Rate, F1, Element Accuracy, Operation F1, cost per call, latency.
  - Drift monitoring with HITL: Motivated by evolving social-media language causing annotation errors; no new experiment in this survey.
- Limitations the authors state:
  - Role-based ensemble orchestrator: Introduces need for communication protocols, risks of conflict or redundancy, and computational overhead.
  - Cascade model routing: Smaller fine-tuned models give cost benefits but often reduced accuracy; latency multi-second per item bottlenecks interactive settings.
  - Agent performance metric suite: Current evaluation practices emphasize accuracy, with limited attention to speed, cost reduction, and long-term sustainability.
  - Drift monitoring with HITL: Outlined as future research; not implemented or evaluated in this survey.
- Limitations they do not state: not assessed. Results are the authors' own, from their simulations, benchmarks or surveys; none evaluates delegation to cheaper models on software work.
